# Brahmajāla Sutta (DN 1 (PTS DN i 1))
**ID:** DN 1 (PTS DN i 1)
**Section:** Dīghanikāya (dn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Brahmajāla Sutta
**PTS:** DN i 1
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/dn1
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0101m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Prompted by conversations between the wanderer Suppiya and his pupil Brahmadatta, the sutta notes that while ordinary people focus on trivial matters such as basic morality when praising or criticizing the Buddha, the Buddha's true teaching penetrates beyond these to systematically classify and dismantle sixty-two contemporary varieties of wrong view (*diṭṭhi*) concerning the past and the future, including eternalism, partial eternalism, and views of supreme *nibbāna* here and now [SuttaCentral; Hirakawa 1990; Bapat and Hirakawa 1970; Eckel 2008; Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995].
Internally, the text shares extensive stock formulas—particularly on monastic ethics—with other early Pali discourses, notably the *Sāmaññaphala Sutta* (DN 2) and the *Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga* (Vb 17), while its sixty-two views closely correspond to the exposition in the *Pañcattaya Sutta* (MN 102), its "middle-length" counterpart [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus; Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995].
